description: Replace the existing Center (Square Butte) and Arrowhead high voltage direct current (HVDC) converter stations and associated assets with modern equipment. To modernize the terminals of the existing Square Butte HVDC Line and implement the latest VSC HVDC technology, new buildings and electrical infrastructure need to be constructed on a new site near the existing HVDC terminals. In Minnesota, to connect the new HVDC terminal to the existing AC system, the Project will require the construction of a new St. Louis County 345 kV/230 kV substation located less than one mile west of the current Arrowhead Substation. The new HVDC terminal will be connected to the St. Louis County Substation by a short 345 kV transmission line, and the new St. Louis County Substation will be connected to the existing Arrowhead Substation by a double-circuit 230 kV transmission line less than one mile in length. Additionally, a short portion of the existing ±250 kV HVDC Line in Minnesota will need to be reconfigured to terminate at the new HVDC terminal. Similar modifications will take place near the existing Center HVDC terminal in North Dakota.

in_service.raw: Minnesota Power filed a combined Certificate of Need and Route Permit Application for the HVDC Modernization Project on June 1, 2023 [Docket Nos. E015/CN-22-607 and E015/TL-22-611], and the Commission granted the Certificate of Need and Route Permit on October 25, 2024. Site development for the converter stations in both Minnesota and North Dakota began in mid-2025, and the Project has a targeted in-service date between April 2029 and April 2030.

name: HVDC Modernization Project

description: The Project consists of approximately 271 miles of new 765 kilovolt (kV) transmission lines across southern Minnesota that will be part of a 765 kV path connecting Minnesota, South Dakota, Iowa, and Wisconsin. The Project also includes approximately 69 miles of a new 345 kV line between the Pleasant Valley, North Rochester and Hampton Substations and modifications at all three 345 kV substations. description: Xcel Energy has applied for a certificate of need and a route permit to construct the Minnesota Energy Connection Project. The project consists of two major components: new substations along with upgrades to existing substations and new 345 kilovolt (kV) high voltage transmission lines (HVTLs). Proposed substation work involves: A new substation to be located near Garvin in Lyon County referred to as the Garvin Substation. An intermediate substation to be located 20 miles north of the proposed Garvin Substation referred to as the Intermediate Substation. A voltage-support substation to be located 80 miles south of the Sherco Substation in either Meeker, Kandiyohi, or Renville County referred to as the Support Substation. Modifications to the existing Sherco Substation and Sherco Solar West Substation near Becker in Sherburne County. Proposed HVTL work involves: A new 345 kV double-circuit HVTL between the Garvin Substation and the existing Sherco Solar West Substation. The applicant’s proposed routes are 171 and 174 miles in length and designated as the Purple Route and Blue Route, respectively. A new 3.1-mile single-circuit 345 kV transmission line between the existing Sherco Solar West Substation and the Sherco Substation referred to as the Green Segment. The Green Segment would be co-located with applicant’s existing Line 5651, occupying the open position on the existing double-circuit-capable structures.

in_service.raw: This project will be in service by October of 2028.

name: Minnesota Energy Connection

raw.Project Name: Rebuild Bingham - Cornell 138 kV
raw.System Need:
•	The Bingham to Cornell 138kV circuit consists of 227 total structures. 17 Lattice Towers, 66 Steel Poles and 144 wood poles installed from 1955 and onward. The average life of the poles is nearing 70 years of age.
•	This project to recommend rebuilding from Bingham Substation to 061I8527. It is recommended to build to current METC 138kV standards which includes steel structures and standard 138kV conductor size. 
•	There have been 12 outages. Those outages consist of 2 lockouts and 10 momentary interruptions. Out of the 12 outages 6 have been caused by storms. 
o	In the last 5 years (2020-2025) this circuit had 4 momentary outages and 1 lockout outage, due to (ice) storms. 
•	There are currently 57 open exceptions for structures that have failed inspections for structural damage, broken/cracked cross arms, bad insulators and bent steel.  
•	This line can be rebuilt from Bingham-Cornell. Doing this will allow METC to not drop the connection to Bluewater Consumers Energy Tap. 
•	Due to the number of exceptions that are written up on the Bingham-Cornell line for aging infrastructure, METC is recommending a full line rebuilt to current 138kV standards.

name: Rebuild Bingham - Cornell 138 kV

raw.Project Name: Rebuild Toll Road - Vital 120kV Line
raw.System Need:
The Toll Rd-Vital 120kV circuit consists of (78) steel poles and (324) wood poles (40%) installed in the late 1990’s and (30%) installed in the 1950’s, the remaining of the poles were installed 1970-1990, which are nearing their end of life. 
In the last (7) years, this circuit has had a total of (2) outages. (1) momentary and (1) lockouts.  Due to operated pole top switches. 
There are currently (214) open exceptions on this line consisting of (urgent) wood pole replacement, leaning pole, guy wire replacement, damaged shield wire, insulator damage, broken insulator bonds and broken interrupters on PTS. 
 - (11) Urgent exceptions consisting of wood pole replacement, split cross arms, and detached static.
There are approximately (75) expectations on this line consisting of wood pole replacement due to resistograph fail, pole rotting, and wood packer damage. 
This line is one of the feeds to the Niles and Seville DTE stations. 
Due to the outage history, maintenance history and current maintenance issues on many of the wood poles on this line, ITCT is recommending a rebuild of the Toll Rd-Vital 120kV line.

name: Rebuild Toll Road - Vital 120kV Line

raw.Project Description:
This project proposes to replace the Mayhew switches (SS280) with a three-position 69 kV breaker station, including any associated line work to reroute the existing lines into the new substation.   It also allows for changing the system normally open point from Duelm Tap 120NSM2 switch to Briggs Lake CBS1 switch to reduce exposure. raw.Project Name: Foley Sub Area Projects
raw.System Need:
A NERC Category P23 (stuck breaker) contingency of the 41RB7 breaker will clear both Benton County 230/69 kV TR13, the Benton County-Milaca 230 kV line, and open-end both the Benton County-Milaca 69 kV line and Benton County-Liberty 69 kV line at Benton County.  This removes both 230 kV sources into the area 69 kV load pocket and makes the 69 kV circuits radially fed, which can cause voltages to approach or exceed limits.  The breaker station will allow the Liberty substation to support the load pocket for this contingency. 

Loss of the Benton County end of the Benton County-Milaca 69 kV line requires specific reconfiguration to minimize the flicker impact of motors starting at ECE’s Pipeline 2 substation while minimizing Delivery Point exposure.  The breaker station will reduce or eliminate this concern. 

Historical momentary and sustained reliability of the Benton County-Milaca 69 kV line has been poor.   

The reliability risk grade for this circuit is an "F" which is an indication that analysis should be done for enhanced sectionalizing. Enhanced sectionalizing can be achieved by adding motors to switches so they can be operated remotely and/or by adding reclosers or breaker stations. 

The reliability grade for this circuit is a "D" which is an indication that analysis should be done to improve reliability. Frequency of outages is driving the poor grade. A breaker station will reduce the frequency of the substation outages by sectionalizing total exposure and load served. 

This circuit has a summer MW-mile value of 1048 and a winter value of 1136, which, while not extreme, are higher than most circuits.  Adding the breaker station will reduce the exposure to the area East Central Energy (ECE) Delivery Points.

name: Foley Sub Area Projects

description: Springfield Public Utilities has requested to interconnect a new substation and load addition to the ITC Midwest transmission system in the city of Springfield, MN.  To support system voltages in the area with the increased load, ITC Midwest will need to upgrade the existing 69 kV capacitor bank at the ITC Midwest owned Waterbury switching station. The Dairyland-Summit 69 kV Project includes:
1. Build a 19-mile, 477 ACSR, 69 kV line to connect the existing East Central Energy’s (ECE) Dairyland and ECE’s Summit substations.
2. Establish a new switch at ECE’s Summit substation with a 3-way, 2000-amp, full-load-break, motor operated 69 kV switch. 
3. Establish a new switch at ECE’s Dairyland substation with a 3-way, 2000-amp, full-load-break, motor operated 69 kV switch.

5. Remove the Fond Du Lac – Summit Tap “DF” 69 kV line (9.92 miles, 2/0 ACSR, 1965) (purple dashed line in graphic below).

The Dairyland-Summit 69 kV Project includes:

2. Establish a new switch at ECE’s Summit substation with a 3-way, 2000-amp, full-load-break, motor operated 69 kV switch. 
3. Establish a new switch at ECE’s Dairyland substation with a 3-way, 2000-amp, full-load-break, motor operated 69 kV switch. 
4. Retire and remove SS-125 (Summit Tap) – FLB switch and motor operators may be able to be reused at another location. 
5. Remove the Fond Du Lac – Summit Tap “DF” 69 kV line (9.92 miles, 2/0 ACSR, 1965) (purple dashed line in graphic below).
6. Retire Fond Du Lac S24 (69/46 kV back-up source to Amnicon, Bardon, and Summit).
raw.Project Name: Dairyland to Summit Area Projects
raw.System Need:
This project will provide looped service to six ECE distribution substations which is needed based on exposure and need to be able to backfeed loads when the main source is lost.

The 69 kV Stinson area loads (Bardon, Amnicon, and Stinson) have a back up source (Fond Du Lac 46/69 kV) which relies on MP’s 46 kV system (23 Line) served between Bear Creek and Thomson H.E.  Minnesota Power has alluded to removing the 23 Line since it is very hard to maintain in the Jay Cooke State Park about 10 years ago and yet to move on the project.  After GRE removes its dependency from the 23 Line, MP can retire the line and GRE can retire Fond Du Lac (S24).

The Fond Du Lac – Summit Tap “DF” 69 kV line (9.92 miles, 2/0 ACSR, 1965) is nearing the end of life and will need rebuilding very soon.  The Dairyland – Summit 69 kV project will remove the dependency on this line and can avoid rebuilding the “DF” line.

The Frog Creek area loads (Wascott, Crystal Lake, and Dairyland) are served from a radial 69 kV system with slight back up from the Dahlberg system (SS-3115).  Connecting to the Dahlberg system has its issues and isn’t an ideal way to back up the Frog Creek area loads.  The Dairyland – Summit 69 kV line will allow for GRE to transfer loads between the Stinson and Frog Creek sources.

The radial MW-mile calculations are:
                           
The threshold for needing to provide a redundant service is 100, so we aren’t justifying the southern end on radial MW-mile alone.  The justification for the project is more based on the avoidance of rebuilding the “DF” line and any future upgrades needed at Fond Du Lac and the looming retirement of the 23 line that sources Fond Du Lac.

description: Indiana Michigan Power (I&M) representatives plan power grid upgrades to improve electric reliability for customers in Noble and Whitley counties. The Albion and Tri-Lakes Improvements Project involves: Rebuilding about 10 miles of 138-kilovolt (kV) transmission line between Kendallville and Albion. Rebuilding about 5 miles of 138-kV transmission line between Albion and Wolf Lake. Rebuilding approximately 9 miles of 138-kV transmission line between Tri-Lakes and Larwill. Replacing substation equipment at the Albion and Kendallville substations. The existing transmission lines include wooden poles and H-frame structures that date back to the 1950s. The power lines are deteriorating and have experienced more than 35 service interruptions since 2015. Rebuilding the power lines with modern steel poles and H-frame structures strengthens the line against weather impacts, reduces frequent maintenance and improves performance. Crews plan to rebuild most of the power line in or near the existing right-of-way, which may require acquiring new or updating existing property easements. Easements are defined land rights that property owners grant the utility to allow for the safe construction, operation and maintenance of the power line.

description: Olive - University Park 345kV Tower Raise LEGEND Olive - University Park 345kV Tower Raise Indiana Michigan Power (I&M) officials plan to upgrade the electric transmission system in Porter, LaPorte and St. Joseph counties, Indiana. The Olive - University Park 345kV Tower Raise involves raising 35 existing transmission towers between the Sedley area in Porter County and New Carlisle in St. Joseph County. Unlike a typical transmission project, the towers will not be replaced. Instead, crews will lift existing steel lattice towers and install new steel sections within the structures, increasing tower heights by approximately 10 to 20 feet. The project increases the distance between the transmission lines and the ground, helping maintain the safe and reliable operation of the electric transmission system. The improvements also address regional transmission needs identified by PJM, the organization responsible for coordinating the flow of electricity across the region.

description: The Barnesville-Summerfield 138-kV Transmission Line Rebuild Project involves rebuilding and upgrading approximately 16 miles of existing power lines. The project traverses Marion and Beaver townships of Noble County, Millwood Township of Guernsey County and Warren Township of Belmont County. The last major reinforcement in this area was done more than 60 years ago. The existing 69-kilovolt (kV) facilities were built in the 1940s. These will be replaced with 138-kV lines and structures that are somewhat taller and of sturdier construction. This will allow the lines to carry more current and help meet customers’ increased demand for power. The company anticipates completion of this project in 2018. The Barnesville-Summerfield 138-kV Transmission Line Rebuild Project will help ensure the continued reliability of the transmission system, which is vital to AEP Transmission’s current customers and supports the development of the area’s economy. AEP anticipates this project, an approximate $20 million investment, will contribute approximately $650,000 in property taxes annually to the community. To request an electronic or paper copy of the Application, please use the comment form at the bottom of this page to make your request.

description: Hopetown 138 kV Extension Transmission Line Project LEGEND Hopetown 138 kV Extension Transmission Line Project AEP Transmission officials plan power grid improvements to enhance electric reliability for customers in Ross County. The upgrades address the growing power demand in the area while relocating transmission facilities away from ancient cultural sites. Crews expect to begin construction in early 2028 and conclude by spring 2029. The project includes: Building Hopetown Substation off Pleasant Valley Road in Chillicothe. Retiring and removing the aging Camp Sherman Substation located off SR 104 in Chillicothe. Building about 2.5 miles of 138-kilovolt (kV) power line* to connect Hopetown Substation to the existing electric grid. *This project requires Ohio Project Siting Board (OPSB) approval. The project aims to meet the increasing power demands of local customers by enhancing the reliability of electric service. Deteriorating structures, nearly a century old, have led to over 4 million minutes of electric service interruptions for customers. By replacing these aging power lines with modern structures, the project seeks to decrease the occurrence of power outages and expedite the restoration process when outages do happen. Additionally, the replacement of the Camp Sherman Substation with the Hopetown Substation enables crews to reroute 2.5 miles of power lines, thereby reducing the impact of transmission facilities on culturally and archaeologically sensitive sites.

description: North Columbus Transmission Line Rebuild Project LEGEND North Columbus Transmission Line Rebuild Project AEP Transmission representatives plan power grid upgrades in Franklin and Delaware counties. The project involves rebuilding about 4.5 miles of power line and upgrading three substations to increase operational performance and capacity of the local electric grid. As project continues to develop, company representatives are changing the construction method for a portion of the power line between Sawmill and Lazelle substations. The regional grid operator PJM Interconnection (PJM) has identified the need for these upgrades to ensure reliable operation of the local electric grid. PJM is the regional transmission organization that coordinates the transportation of bulk electricity across a 13-state region.

description: (Phase 2) South Coshocton–Wooster Transmission Line Rebuild Project (Phase 2): AEP Transmission representatives plan to rebuild approximately 40 miles of 138‑kV transmission line to improve electric reliability for customers in Coshocton, Holmes and Wayne counties. Structure No. 51 will be relocated approximately 120 feet to the west and along the same centerline as its existing location and be replaced with a single steel monopole on concrete foundation. Structure No. 52 will be relocated approximately 50 feet to the west and along the same centerline as its existing location and be replaced with a Valmont pyramax tower on concrete foundations. Structure No. 53 will be relocated to the inside of the existing Lapier 69 kV Substation and replaced with a Valmont pyramax tower on concrete foundations. description: Update At FirstEnergy, it is our responsibility to deliver the power our customers depend on in their daily lives. Keystone Appalachian Transmission Company (“KATCo”), a FirstEnergy company, has identified a need for a new 138-kilovolt (kV) transmission line in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, to enhance service reliability for distribution customers. KATCo evaluated the existing transmission system in the area and identified the need to construct a new 138-kV transmission line to connect the existing Ethel Springs Substation to the existing Bethlen Substation.
